anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Roast and eat the flesh — the Passover act the passion did not perform.

pass_a_gloss: For we must sacrifice the true sheep, if we have been made priests or offer equally with the priests, and we must roast and we must eat his flesh. And this upon the Savior's passion if it has not happened, then his passion is not a type of the pascha, but a type of Christ himself the pascha becomes, of the one sacrificed by us.
pass_b_english: For we must sacrifice the true sheep, if we have been made priests or offer equally with the priests, and we must roast and eat his flesh. And if this has not happened in the passion of the Savior, then his passion is not a type of the Passover. The Passover becomes a type of Christ himself, who is sacrificed by us (Exodus 12:8–9) (1 Peter 2:5).
